To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) inpatient cardiology staff are poor at recording family history; and 2) a family tree obtained by specialist allied health staff can reveal familial cardiac disease in a significant proportion of patients.

inpatient cardiological services fail to recognize the familial nature of many ‘idiopathic’ conditions, and that a family history taken by a specially trained allied health professional is more likely to detect a familial diagnosis.
